newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS STEADY-OFF $1 - PRIVATE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS STEADY-OFF $1 - PRIVATE.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Wednesday were steady to $1.00 per cwt lower on continued hefty hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $56.00 to $56.50 in the country and $57.00 to $57.50 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 lower at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 at plants.
"Everyone seems to be getting enough hogs this morning," a central Illinois buyer said.
Indiana dealers said hog marketings continued brisk despite lower prices this week. Indiana hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $54.00 to $54.50 in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 at plants.
"They're keeping us pretty busy today," one Indiana livestock dealer said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants.
Pork prices were only marginally lower despite a recent increase in slaughter, which suggested that demand could be improving, market sources said.
